slides.headline: What's the real difference?
slides.body: Full doc lending relies on two or more years of accountant-prepared financials, giving lenders more confidence and often better pricing. Low doc lending replaces this with reduced evidence like bank statements or BAS lodgements, it still requires proof of income, just in a different form.

caption:
Full doc and low doc aren't a hierarchy of 'proper' versus 'lesser' lending, they're two different ways of demonstrating the same thing: that your business can service the loan.

Full doc uses complete financials to unlock potentially sharper terms. Low doc accepts alternative evidence like bank statements or BAS lodgements for businesses whose income doesn't fit a standard template, but it always still requires evidence of income.

General information only. This does not constitute financial, legal, accounting or tax advice. Credit is subject to lender assessment, eligibility and approval criteria. Fees, charges, terms and conditions may apply.
